facts.text: Director Antonio Margheriti is credited as 'Anthony M. Dawson', star Marina Giulia Cavalli as 'Julia Mc. Kay' and Luciano Pigozzi as 'Alan Collins'. Italian B-movies loved fake English names.
Director Antonio Margheriti's other pseudonym was 'Antony Daisies' — a pun, since 'margherite' is Italian for daisies.
Director Antonio Margheriti made this right after churning out Raiders of the Lost Ark knockoffs, and back-to-back with his two 'Indio' action films starring boxing champ Marvelous Marvin Hagler.
The jungle scenes were shot in Pagsanjan, Laguna, in the Philippines, with other work done in Latina, Italy. The film premiered in the Philippines on May 27, 1989.
Jane's English voice isn't Marina Giulia Cavalli's. Carolyn De Fonseca dubbed her. De Fonseca was also Olga in Suspiria and voiced Jayne Mansfield after Mansfield's death.
Luciano Pigozzi (Dr. Geoffrey) was nicknamed 'the Italian Peter Lorre' for his looks. He acted in 17 films for director Antonio Margheriti and more than 100 overall.
Margheriti was nearly 70 when he made this, and the film is widely called an Alien (1979) ripoff. Critic reviews note its 1950s-style atomic-monster plot in an 80s creature-feature wrapper.
The title sounds like a James Cameron cash-in, but The Abyss opened in the US in August 1989. Director Antonio Margheriti's film had already premiered in the Philippines that May.
Director Antonio Margheriti studied engineering at university and became a specialist in optical effects and model-making. That explains the miniature-heavy action in his films.
Director Antonio Margheriti sped up shoots by running several cameras at once. That let him capture master shots and close-ups in one take and make multiple films a year.
The helicopters, jeeps, boats and wheel loaders in the action scenes are often miniatures. Director Antonio Margheriti was a model-effects expert.
One reviewer singled out the helicopter action: a dive out of a chopper, with a dummy and a real stunt performer sharing the fall.
Charles Napier (Colonel Kovacks) also played country singer Tucker McElroy in The Blues Brothers (1980) — and once signed autographs as 'McElroy' when fans asked.
Much of the score is recycled from Robert O. Ragland's music for Larry Cohen's monster movie Q, the Winged Serpent (1982).
Daniel Bosch plays Bob, the snake farmer who 'milks' venom for drug companies. He later became a pastor for the Worldwide Church of God in Sardinia, Italy.
Edoardo Margheriti, son of director Antonio Margheriti, worked on this film as assistant director. He later made a 2013 documentary about his father.
Charles Napier provided the growls for TV's The Incredible Hulk (1977) and played a space hippie named Adam in the Star Trek episode 'The Way to Eden.'
Screenwriter Tito Carpi also wrote the killer-octopus movie Tentacles (1977) and the sci-fi action films Escape from the Bronx and Raiders of Atlantis (both 1983).
The gruesome radiation-burn effects on the lake divers are among the film's most praised practical gore.
The monster, 'Big Claw', is a puppet over 25 feet (7 m) tall. Critics note the creature is never seen as anything but a giant claw until the finale.
The creature effects were made from 'tubing, wire, and other materials you could pick up at your local hardware shop.' IMDb says Big Claw was built from drainage pipe and plastic trays.
Stanley Kubrick reportedly wanted director Antonio Margheriti's help on 2001: A Space Odyssey. Margheriti only visited the set and talked shop with Kubrick and effects chief Douglas Trumbull.
Luciano Pigozzi's credits include Mario Bava's Blood and Black Lace (1964) and the goriest of his roles in Baron Blood. His career ran from 1954 to 1989.
Director Antonio Margheriti's Yor, the Hunter from the Future (1983) was among his most financially successful films, despite mostly poor reviews on release.
Dr. Geoffrey's 'gas that absorbs liquid hydrogen' is pseudo-science: hydrogen only liquefies at around -400°F or colder, so it couldn't be sitting around underground.
This Italian-Filipino co-production was shot in English, then re-voiced in post-production. That's why some performers sound different from how they look.
Director Antonio Margheriti shot to look old-school on purpose: '70s-style cameras, exploding miniatures, and framing the monster around corners or through fog.
Before gothic classics like Castle of Blood, director Antonio Margheriti was known for horror and westerns. Mondo Digital calls this film 'the perfect 80s Italian popcorn flick.'
One critic calls the creature a rejiggered H.R. Giger design with parts from the nearest auto garage. It was built by Philippine technicians.
Charles Napier was a former Army man, sports coach and art teacher before acting. His first big film role was in Russ Meyer's Cherry, Harry & Raquel! (1969).
No power-loader armor like Aliens here. On a tiny budget, director Antonio Margheriti has his heroes fight the monster with bulldozers.
